short: Face voices (M08) extend 2020 TTS and 2023 lip-to-speech designs to EMG; the pitch-flattening gain (M02) is within seed noise; silent WER 38.91% has no external baseline.
position: The paper [@lee2025speaking] changes two components: the voice comes from a face image instead of reference audio (M08), and the EMG encoder's ContentVec target from pitch-flattened speech (M02). M08 is standard: face-image voice control dates to 2020 in text-to-speech (cited, §II-B) and 2023 in lip-to-speech [@sheng2023zeroshot; @choi2023diffv2s]; only the transfer to EMG is new. M02 is standard: flattening lowers silent WER from 40.12% to 38.91% but raises voiced CER from 9.96% to 13.28% (Table I), with no repeated training runs on one EMG speaker. The evaluation (M12) is behind: only the paper's own two variants are compared, while earlier work on the same split and ASR reports a published model, at 30.0% WER in the recorded speaker's voice [@ren2024diffets]. The cost of face-chosen voices is never separated from vocoder and content-estimator error. Audio-free multi-speaker voicing holds, and the face predicts global pitch beyond gender (Table III); timbre beyond gender and effective pitch disentanglement remain unsupported.
